103 |
    104 |
  • Build a single-player rhythm game called midi_mover.
    • 105 |

    • 106 |
  • Head center is the midpoint between the two eye keypoints.
    • 107 |
  • Gameplay interaction events must be driven by fingertips from the hand-keypoint model, not by wrist keypoints from the body model.

    • 111 |
  • Gameplay notes are tokens L1..L5 and R1..R5. L means left hand must enter the circle. R means right hand must enter the circle.
    • 112 |
  • Target songs are loaded from a folder of MIDI files. On startup, choose a random MIDI. After each song, choose another random MIDI.
    • 113 |
  • Audio quality is a first-class gameplay requirement: target-song playback should support expressive, high-quality instrument timbres (not only basic beeps/sine cues).

    • 116 |
  • Show the MIDI-derived song title before starting each song. The title is extracted from the MIDI filename, not from MIDI metadata.
    • 117 |

    • 118 |

369 | def _build_tick_to_seconds_converter(*, merged_track: Any, ticks_per_beat: int, mido_module: Any) -> Any:
370 |     tempo_changes: list[tuple[int, int]] = [(0, DEFAULT_TEMPO_US_PER_BEAT)]
371 |     absolute_tick = 0
372 | 
373 |     for message in merged_track:
374 |         delta_ticks = int(message.time)
375 |         if delta_ticks < 0:
376 |             raise MidiParseError(f"Encountered negative delta tick ({delta_ticks}) while building tempo map.")
377 |         absolute_tick += delta_ticks
378 | 
379 |         if getattr(message, "type", None) == "set_tempo":
380 |             tempo_changes.append((absolute_tick, int(message.tempo)))
381 | 
382 |     normalized_tempo_changes: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
383 |     for tick, tempo in sorted(tempo_changes, key=lambda item: item[0]):
384 |         if normalized_tempo_changes and normalized_tempo_changes[-1][0] == tick:
385 |             normalized_tempo_changes[-1] = (tick, tempo)
386 |         else:
387 |             normalized_tempo_changes.append((tick, tempo))
388 | 
389 |     tempo_ticks = [tick for tick, _ in normalized_tempo_changes]
390 |     tempo_values = [tempo for _, tempo in normalized_tempo_changes]
391 | 
392 |     cumulative_seconds: list[float] = [0.0]
393 |     for index in range(1, len(tempo_ticks)):
394 |         previous_tick = tempo_ticks[index - 1]
395 |         current_tick = tempo_ticks[index]
396 |         delta_ticks = current_tick - previous_tick
397 |         cumulative_seconds.append(
398 |             cumulative_seconds[index - 1]
399 |             + float(
400 |                 mido_module.tick2second(
401 |                     delta_ticks,
402 |                     ticks_per_beat=ticks_per_beat,
403 |                     tempo=tempo_values[index - 1],
404 |                 )
405 |             )
406 |         )
407 | 
408 |     def tick_to_seconds(tick: int) -> float:
409 |         if tick < 0:
410 |             raise MidiParseError(f"Cannot convert negative absolute tick ({tick}) to seconds.")
411 |         segment_index = bisect_right(tempo_ticks, tick) - 1
412 |         if segment_index < 0:
413 |             segment_index = 0
414 |         segment_tick = tempo_ticks[segment_index]
415 |         segment_tempo = tempo_values[segment_index]
416 |         extra_ticks = tick - segment_tick
417 |         return cumulative_seconds[segment_index] + float(
418 |             mido_module.tick2second(
419 |                 extra_ticks,
420 |                 ticks_per_beat=ticks_per_beat,
421 |                 tempo=segment_tempo,
422 |             )
423 |         )
424 | 
425 |     return tick_to_seconds

510 | def _build_adaptive_note_mapping(
511 |     *,
512 |     playable_notes: tuple[PlayableMidiNote, ...],
513 | ) -> dict[int, str]:
514 |     """Build deterministic note->token mapping that can collapse many notes to 10 tokens.
515 | 
516 |     The mapping is assigned in first-seen time order and wraps after the ten
517 |     gesture tokens, allowing multiple source note numbers to share a token.
518 |     """
519 | 
520 |     note_mapping: dict[int, str] = {}
521 |     next_token_index = 0
522 |     for playable_note in playable_notes:
523 |         note_number = playable_note.note_number
524 |         if note_number in note_mapping:
525 |             continue
526 |         note_mapping[note_number] = GESTURE_TOKENS[next_token_index % len(GESTURE_TOKENS)]
527 |         next_token_index += 1
528 |     return note_mapping

def _load_simple_yaml(raw_text: str, config_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Parse a minimal YAML subset when PyYAML is unavailable.

    Supported features:
    - nested mappings by indentation
    - scalar values: strings, ints, floats, bools, null
    - inline lists like [1, 2] or [".mid", ".midi"]
    """
    root: dict[str, Any] = {}
    stack: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]] = [(-1, root)]

    for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(raw_text.splitlines(), start=1):
        line = raw_line.split("#", 1)[0].rstrip()
        if not line.strip():
            continue

        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
        if indent % 2 != 0:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: line {line_number} uses unsupported indentation."
            )

        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("- "):
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: block list syntax is unsupported by the built-in YAML fallback on line {line_number}."
            )

        key, sep, value = stripped.partition(":")
        if not sep:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: expected 'key: value' on line {line_number}."
            )

        while len(stack) > 1 and indent <= stack[-1][0]:
            stack.pop()

        current = stack[-1][1]
        key = key.strip()
        value = value.strip()
        if not key:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: empty key on line {line_number}."
            )

        if value == "":
            child: dict[str, Any] = {}
            current[key] = child
            stack.append((indent, child))
        else:
            current[key] = _parse_scalar(value)

    return root


def _parse_scalar(value: str) -> Any:
    lowered = value.lower()
    if lowered == "true":
        return True
    if lowered == "false":
        return False
    if lowered in {"null", "none"}:
        return None

    if value.startswith("[") and value.endswith("]"):
        inner = value[1:-1].strip()
        if not inner:
            return []
        return [_parse_scalar(part.strip()) for part in inner.split(",")]

    if (value.startswith('"') and value.endswith('"')) or (
        value.startswith("'") and value.endswith("'")
    ):
        return ast.literal_eval(value)

    try:
        return int(value)
    except ValueError:
        pass

    try:
        return float(value)
    except ValueError:
        pass

    return value


def _normalize_mapping_key(key: Any) -> str:
    text = str(key)
    if (text.startswith('"') and text.endswith('"')) or (
        text.startswith("'") and text.endswith("'")
    ):
        return text[1:-1]
    return text

midi_mover Implementation Backlog

This document is the single source of implementation instructions for a later coding agent. It contains the required scope, architecture guidance, epics, tasks, subtasks, definitions of done, and workflow rules. Do not assume hidden requirements outside this page.

All items start as TODO. When a subtask is fully complete, change its label to DONE. If all subtasks in a task are done, set the task to DONE. If all tasks in an epic are done, set the epic to DONE.

Global product definition

  • Build a single-player rhythm game called midi_mover.
  • Use a two-stage Ultralytics pipeline: stage 1 body/pose detection for person + eye anchors, and stage 2 hand-keypoint detection on a person-ROI crop. Do not build separate custom detectors outside Ultralytics models.
  • Head center is the midpoint between the two eye keypoints.
  • Gameplay interaction events must be driven by fingertips from the hand-keypoint model, not by wrist keypoints from the body model.
  • The gameplay screen is split into 60% live camera view on the left and 40% note timeline on the right.
  • The live camera view must crop around the player, stretch to full panel height while preserving aspect ratio, and pad left/right as needed to fill the panel width.
  • There are 5 circles around the head. Their fixed semantic numbering is: 1 = far left, 2 = upper-left, 3 = above head, 4 = upper-right, 5 = far right.
  • Gameplay notes are tokens L1..L5 and R1..R5. L means left hand must enter the circle. R means right hand must enter the circle.
  • Target songs are loaded from a folder of MIDI files. On startup, choose a random MIDI. After each song, choose another random MIDI.
  • Audio quality is a first-class gameplay requirement: target-song playback should support expressive, high-quality instrument timbres (not only basic beeps/sine cues).
  • The right panel is a Guitar-Hero-like waterfall timeline with 5 vertical lanes. Notes move from top to bottom. The horizontal “now” line is fixed at 25% of panel height from the top.
  • After notes are judged, they remain visible below the now line and are colored green on hit and red on miss.
  • Show the MIDI-derived song title before starting each song. The title is extracted from the MIDI filename, not from MIDI metadata.
  • At the end of every song, show result summary and the highscore board. If the result qualifies for a new highscore entry, show a countdown from 3 to 0, take a new headshot, save it, and show the updated board.
  • The highscore board must always show score and percentage of notes hit, even when the just-finished run is not a new entry.

Mandatory workflow rules for the later agent

  • Always fulfill each subtask completely before moving to the next one.
  • Use the conda environment midi_mover.
  • After each completed subtask, the complete pipeline must run. “Complete pipeline” means the app must launch, load config, open the camera, initialize the window, load at least one MIDI file, render the liveview/timeline composition, and exit cleanly without regressions. Use a minimal smoke-test path if the full interactive flow is not practical in automated mode.
  • After fulfilling a subtask, update this TODO.html file immediately and set that subtask to DONE.
  • If all subtasks under a task are done, set the task to DONE.
  • If all tasks under an epic are done, set the epic to DONE.
  • Do not use git. Do not create commits, branches, tags, or Git metadata.
  • Keep the project runnable from one explicit entry point, for example:
    python main.py --camera_id 0 --midi_dir ./midi --config ./config/default.yaml
  • Do not hardcode magic numbers in source files. All tuneable values must live in a YAML config file.

Configuration requirement: all hyperparameters must live in YAML

Create a dedicated YAML configuration file, for example config/default.yaml, and load it at startup. The later agent may add more keys, but at minimum the YAML must own all tuneable values from the list below.

Application and runtime

  • window width, height, target FPS
  • debug flags
  • logging level
  • random seed behavior

Camera and pose

  • camera width, height, mirror on/off
  • Ultralytics stage-1 model path/name
  • Ultralytics stage-2 hand-keypoint model path/name
  • pose confidence threshold
  • IOU threshold
  • device selection (CPU/GPU)
  • stage-2 ROI expansion in pixels around detected person bbox (default 30px each side)
  • tracking smoothing factors
  • lost-person timeout and fallback behavior

Liveview layout and circles

  • left/right panel ratio
  • crop margins around person
  • circle radius
  • circle offsets relative to head center
  • circle stroke width
  • label font sizes
  • padding color

Gameplay and judgment

  • hit window in milliseconds
  • early/late tolerance
  • debounce timing for fingertip-in-circle events
  • fingertip trigger policy (which fingertips can trigger, per-hand/per-finger options)
  • note history duration below the now line
  • lookahead duration above the now line
  • score values, combo bonuses, miss penalties
  • debug overlays for full keypoint rendering from stage-1 and stage-2 models

MIDI and mapping

  • supported MIDI extensions
  • note-number to gesture-token mapping
  • optional dynamic/adaptive note-to-circle mapping mode
  • rolling note-history buffer size for adaptive mapping (for example last 30 notes)
  • track/channel filtering rules
  • minimum note duration thresholds
  • ignored meta events and unsupported-note policy

Audio, summary, and highscore

  • audio backend selection (pygame or pyfluidsynth)
  • backend-specific low-latency settings (buffer, sample rate, channels)
  • SoundFont (.sf2) path and loading policy for FluidSynth
  • MIDI channel/program handling and optional instrument override profiles
  • FluidSynth mix controls: gain, polyphony, reverb, chorus
  • volumes for cue, hit, and UI sounds; plus target-song playback gain
  • fallback audio behavior when preferred backend is unavailable
  • highscore list size
  • headshot countdown duration
  • headshot crop margins
  • thumbnail dimensions

Rule: if a later agent needs to tune something during implementation, that value must be moved into YAML instead of being left inline in code.

Assumptions that the later agent must preserve

  • Single visible player only. If multiple people appear, pick one primary person consistently and ignore the others.
  • The camera ID and MIDI folder path are external inputs, not hardcoded.
  • MIDI parsing is done with mido.
  • Audio playback uses a pluggable backend. Preferred target-song renderer is pyfluidsynth (SoundFont-based), with pygame retained as a compatibility fallback.
  • Runtime window rendering is done with pygame.
  • The live camera stream can be processed with OpenCV and then blitted into pygame surfaces.
  • All note-to-gesture mapping must be configurable in YAML. The implementation must not assume arbitrary MIDI files are naturally playable without mapping.

def load_config(config_path: Path) -> AppConfig:
    """Load and validate the application YAML config."""
    raw_text = config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if yaml is not None:
        try:
            payload = yaml.safe_load(raw_text)
        except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: {exc}"
            ) from exc
    else:
        payload = _load_simple_yaml(raw_text, config_path)

    if payload is None:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"Config file {config_path} is empty. Add the required startup keys."
        )
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise ConfigError(
            f"Config file {config_path} must contain a top-level mapping/object."
        )

    _validate_required_paths(payload)
    _validate_value_types(payload)
    return AppConfig(raw=payload)


def _validate_required_paths(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    missing = []
    for path in REQUIRED_PATHS:
        if not _has_path(payload, path):
            missing.append(".".join(path))

    if missing:
        joined = "\n - ".join([""] + missing)
        raise ConfigError(
            "Config is missing required keys:" + joined + "\nAdd them to the YAML file and retry startup."
        )


def _has_path(payload: dict[str, Any], path: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    current: Any = payload
    for segment in path:
        if not isinstance(current, dict) or segment not in current:
            return False
        current = current[segment]
    return True

def _require_type(value: Any, expected_type: type, name: str) -> None:
    if not isinstance(value, expected_type):
        raise ConfigError(
            f"Config key {name} must be of type {expected_type.__name__}, got {type(value).__name__}."
        )


def _require_non_empty_string(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
    _require_type(value, str, name)
    if not value.strip():
        raise ConfigError(f"Config key {name} must be a non-empty string.")


def _require_optional_type(value: Any, expected_type: type, name: str) -> None:
    if value is not None and not isinstance(value, expected_type):
        raise ConfigError(
            f"Config key {name} must be null or {expected_type.__name__}, got {type(value).__name__}."
        )


def _require_numeric(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
    if not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or isinstance(value, bool):
        raise ConfigError(f"Config key {name} must be numeric, got {type(value).__name__}.")


def _require_vector2(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
    if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) != 2:
        raise ConfigError(f"Config key {name} must be a 2-item list [x, y].")
    for index, item in enumerate(value):
        _require_numeric(item, f"{name}[{index}]")


def _require_color_triplet(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
    if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) != 3:
        raise ConfigError(f"Config key {name} must be an RGB triplet like [0, 0, 0].")
    for index, item in enumerate(value):
        _require_type(item, int, f"{name}[{index}]")
        if not 0 <= item <= 255:
            raise ConfigError(f"Config key {name}[{index}] must be between 0 and 255.")

    required_tokens = ("L1", "L2", "L3", "L4", "L5", "R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5")
    normalized = {_normalize_mapping_key(key): value for key, value in gesture_sounds.items()}
    gesture_sounds.clear()
    gesture_sounds.update(normalized)

    if sorted(normalized.keys()) != sorted(required_tokens):
        raise ConfigError(
            "audio.gesture_sounds must define exactly the gesture tokens "
            "L1, L2, L3, L4, L5, R1, R2, R3, R4, and R5."
        )

    for token in required_tokens:
        spec = normalized[token]
        _require_type(spec, dict, f"audio.gesture_sounds.{token}")
        if "frequency_hz" not in spec:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Config key audio.gesture_sounds.{token}.frequency_hz is required."
            )
        if "waveform" not in spec:
            raise ConfigError(f"Config key audio.gesture_sounds.{token}.waveform is required.")
        _require_numeric(spec["frequency_hz"], f"audio.gesture_sounds.{token}.frequency_hz")
        _require_type(spec["waveform"], str, f"audio.gesture_sounds.{token}.waveform")


def _load_simple_yaml(raw_text: str, config_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Parse a minimal YAML subset when PyYAML is unavailable.

    Supported features:
    - nested mappings by indentation
    - scalar values: strings, ints, floats, bools, null
    - inline lists like [1, 2] or [".mid", ".midi"]
    """
    root: dict[str, Any] = {}
    stack: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]] = [(-1, root)]

    for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(raw_text.splitlines(), start=1):
        line = raw_line.split("#", 1)[0].rstrip()
        if not line.strip():
            continue

        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
        if indent % 2 != 0:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: line {line_number} uses unsupported indentation."
            )

        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("- "):
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: block list syntax is unsupported by the built-in YAML fallback on line {line_number}."
            )

        key, sep, value = stripped.partition(":")
        if not sep:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: expected 'key: value' on line {line_number}."
            )

        while len(stack) > 1 and indent <= stack[-1][0]:
            stack.pop()

        current = stack[-1][1]
        key = key.strip()
        value = value.strip()
        if not key:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"Failed to parse YAML config at {config_path}: empty key on line {line_number}."
            )

        if value == "":
            child: dict[str, Any] = {}
            current[key] = child
            stack.append((indent, child))
        else:
            current[key] = _parse_scalar(value)

    return root


def _parse_scalar(value: str) -> Any:
    lowered = value.lower()
    if lowered == "true":
        return True
    if lowered == "false":
        return False
    if lowered in {"null", "none"}:
        return None

    if value.startswith("[") and value.endswith("]"):
        inner = value[1:-1].strip()
        if not inner:
            return []
        return [_parse_scalar(part.strip()) for part in inner.split(",")]

    if (value.startswith('"') and value.endswith('"')) or (
        value.startswith("'") and value.endswith("'")
    ):
        return ast.literal_eval(value)

    try:
        return int(value)
    except ValueError:
        pass

    try:
        return float(value)
    except ValueError:
        pass

    return value


def _normalize_mapping_key(key: Any) -> str:
    text = str(key)
    if (text.startswith('"') and text.endswith('"')) or (
        text.startswith("'") and text.endswith("'")
    ):
        return text[1:-1]
    return text
